chunks: Abū Muḥammad Hārūn ibn Mūsā Al-Tal’ukbari narrated to me from Abī ‘Ali Muḥammad ibn Hammām ibn Suhayl, from Aḥmad ibn Mābundād, from Aḥmad ibn Mu’āfā Al-Tha’labi, from the people of Ra’s Al-‘Ayn, from ‘Ali ibn Ja’far Al-Humāni, who said:

I heard ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad Al-‘Askari (peace be upon him) say: Whoever leaves his home intending to perform the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (peace be upon him), and goes to the Euphrates and performs Ghusl with its water, Allāh will record him among the successful. And when he says Salām to Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), Allāh will record him among the winners. And when he finishes his prayer, an angel will come to him and say: Verily the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) conveys his Salām to you and tells you: As for your sins, they have been forgiven to you; start again with the deeds.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for performing Ghusl in the Euphrates before visiting Imam Husain?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the Euphrates as a sacred locus of purification, linking the physical act of Ghusl to spiritual triumph. The narrative culminates in a direct transmission of greetings from the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.) via an angel, affirming the pilgrim's sins are forgiven and inviting a fresh start in worship, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt.
